Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Regional Konongo traffic gridlock: Motorists lose hours as authorities promise relief in 3 weeks Source : Myjoyonline 17 November 2026 11:39am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Motorists and commuters travelling along the Konongo-Kumasi-Accra highway are spending more than two hours navigating severe traffic congestion, with authorities promising relief within three weeks.
The persistent gridlock has reduced movement to a crawl, leaving vehicles bumper-to-bumper as frustrated commuters struggle to get through the busy stretch.
The congestion has disrupted journeys along the major highway, affecting commercial drivers, private motorists and passengers who rely on the route for travel between Kumasi and Accra.
Authorities have attributed the situation to roadside trading activities by market women who have refused to relocate to a newly constructed market, as well as a pothole along a critical section of the road.
The continued presence of traders along the roadside has reportedly restricted available space for vehicles, while the damaged section has further slowed traffic movement.
The situation is compounded by the volume of vehicles using Konongo as a major transit point, including commercial vehicles travelling from neighbouring countries such as Togo and Burkina Faso.
Beyond the delays, motorists have raised concerns about road safety, citing narrow sections of the highway, poorly managed intersections, numerous potholes and the absence of adequate road signs.
One motorist described the area as dangerous, warning that the combination of heavy traffic and inadequate road infrastructure was exposing road users to accidents.
"The intersections at the station create congestion. It's dangerous to be around this road. Konongo Road is always busy," the motorist said.
The motorist also pointed to the frequent movement of drivers from Togo and Burkina Faso, saying their use of the route added to the congestion.
"Togo and Burkina drivers all ply this area, creating the congestion and the road is too narrow. We are witnessing too many accidents, so many potholes and there are no road signs. Every day Konongo is busy," the motorist added.
The concerns reflect the growing frustration among road users, many of whom face lengthy delays on a highway that serves as an important link for passenger and commercial transportation.
Authorities have, however, assured motorists that measures are expected to ease the congestion within three weeks.
The promised intervention is expected to address the immediate challenges contributing to the gridlock, particularly roadside trading activities and the damaged section of the road.
For commuters and commercial drivers who depend on the Konongo-Kumasi-Accra highway, the hope is that the intervention will restore smoother traffic movement, reduce travel delays and improve safety along the route.
